newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court jails neo-Nazi for murder and rape.
newsitem.headline: German court jails neo-Nazi for murder and rape.

text.p: A 28-year-old German neo-Nazi, who claimed the Norse god of war Odin had ordered him to kill, was found guilty on Tuesday of murder and rape and sentenced to life imprisonment.

Thomas Lemke, who belonged to several extreme right-wing groups in western Germany, was convicted of killing a former friend with a shotgun and murdering two young women. He was also found guilty on one count of rape and attempted rape.

Lemke, from the western town of Gladbeck, confessed to committing the murders between mid-1995 and March 1996, and said he had also killed two other women and a former friend although police found no evidence of these supposed crimes.

The court in Essen decided that, because of the gravity of his crimes, Lemke should be detained in a psychiatric hospital after he completes the jail term. A life sentence in Germany is normally 15 years.

Lemke's 26-year-old girlfriend, named only as Bianca W., was convicted of complicity in the first murder and jailed for six years. A 26-year-old friend, Marcel M., was found guilty of complicity to rape and murder and given five years in jail.
The court found that Lemke had raped one of the victims, an English woman, and attempted to rape his other murder victim, a German woman, before he killed them.

The court heard Lemke was involved in an extreme right-wing group of self-styled "Vikings" who worshipped the god Odin. During the two-month trial he described how he received orders from Odin to kill.
Lemke claimed he had committed the first murder to bind his girlfriend Bianca W. closer to him by getting her involved in the crime but the rest were carried out under orders from Odin.

"I must have been mad. I'm sorry. I cannot find any excuse. If I could give my life so that she (the first victim) was alive again then I would do so immediately," Lemke told the court during his trial, when asked how he felt about the crimes.
